parsed.attack: The demand is litigation rather than guilt, and litigation demand is spiky rather than standing: it peaks in the weeks before a hearing and evaporates the moment an order is made, so nightly logging for months is being asked of people whose motivation is episodic. There is also a motive mismatch - the parent in a high-conflict case wants evidence about the other parent's failures, not a diary of their own bedtimes, and a contemporaneous record of one's own compliance is the thing lawyers ask for and clients resent producing.
parsed.strongest_defence: This audience already pays for a court-mandated co-parenting app and demonstrably free-types the same observations into calendar notes [214], which is costly manual behaviour performed under adversarial pressure rather than a stated wish; documentation spend in family law is one of the few consumer categories with proven, non-discretionary willingness to pay, and the practitioner referral loop attaches the product to the moment the motivation is highest.
parsed.verdict_reason: The demand is legal jeopardy backed by an existing paid mandate and an observed manual workaround, which is the opposite of pain that is stated but not felt.
